counting_rule: Nine distinct official document URLs; sections of one specification are counted once. Navigation-only views are not counted as reading.
method: Direct web opens and targeted section opens. Official documentation only; no code observation, product execution, user testing, or AI decomposition experiments.

sources.title: arc42 — Introduction and Goals
sources.read_scope: Sections 1.1 Requirements Overview, 1.2 Quality Goals, 1.3 Stakeholder; web lines 43–112
sources.observed: Short requirements summaries should link to existing requirements. Business goals, essential functions, architecture quality goals, and stakeholder expectations are distinct. Project goals are not necessarily architecture quality goals.
sources.input_inference: Keep the original purpose and its source distinct from extracted interpretation; do not conflate delivery deadlines with runtime quality requirements.
sources.limitations: Architecture documentation guidance, not an evaluated retrieval input interface. It does not justify requiring a complete stakeholder table for a narrow partial question.

sources.title: arc42 — Architecture Constraints
sources.observed: Constraints limit design, implementation, or development choices; they can extend beyond a system and may be negotiable. Simple explanatory tables are proposed.
sources.input_inference: Distinguish mandatory constraints from preferences and negotiable choices; current technology use does not itself mean alternatives are forbidden.
sources.limitations: No required input field set or strictness taxonomy is prescribed. Negotiability cannot override an explicit user prohibition.

sources.title: arc42 — Context and Scope
sources.read_scope: Introduction, 3.1 Business context, 3.2 Technical context; web lines 43–110
sources.observed: System boundaries and communication partners define external interfaces. Domain inputs/outputs may be separated from technical channels, protocols, and hardware, with mappings between them. Tables can substitute for diagrams.
sources.input_inference: For a selected part, retain immediate inputs/outputs, surrounding actors, and change boundaries where known; do not invent technical channels from domain flows.
sources.limitations: A complete architecture documentation expectation cannot be assumed to be a prerequisite for exploratory partial search. Runtime paths and success are not verified.

sources.title: C4 model — System context diagram
sources.read_scope: Introduction, Scope, Primary and Supporting elements, Recommended; web lines 35–60
sources.observed: A system context diagram scopes one system among people and directly connected external systems. It emphasizes a broad view rather than technologies and protocols.
sources.input_inference: Preserve the abstraction level. A protocol omitted from an overview is unknown, not absent or inferable.
sources.limitations: This diagram purpose does not justify forcing a complete C4 hierarchy for a function-level or mechanism-only question. Context alone cannot establish interface compatibility.

sources.title: C4 model — Dynamic diagram
sources.read_scope: Introduction, Scope, Recommended, Notes; web lines 35–61
sources.observed: Dynamic diagrams depict how static model elements collaborate in a specific feature/use case, optionally with numbered ordering. They may use system, container, or component level and should be used selectively for interesting or complicated interactions.
sources.input_inference: Separate an example path from the whole architecture; unshown paths are not automatically absent, and a pictured path is not automatically unconditional.
sources.limitations: Diagram guidance is not runtime observation. It does not establish ordering in an unnumbered structural diagram or justify mandatory dynamic diagrams.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification 3.1.1
sources.read_scope: Introduction, 4.8.10 Operation Object, 4.8.18 Callback Object, 4.8.20 Link Object. Entire 4,243-line specification was not read.
sources.observed: Describes HTTP APIs. operationId is unique within the described API. Callbacks relate to parent operations; independent incoming requests use webhooks. Link Objects represent possible design-time links and do not guarantee successful invocation.
sources.input_inference: Keep request actors, callback recipients, and relationship evidence distinct. Do not promote an API relation into observed execution, successful operation, or a user's purpose.
sources.limitations: No particular server was executed. Descriptions and external documentation can encode intent; saying OpenAPI cannot contain any intent would be incorrect.

sources.title: AsyncAPI Specification 3.0.0
sources.read_scope: Introduction, Operation Object, Operation Reply Object, Correlation ID Object. Entire 2,305-line specification was not read.
sources.observed: Specifies an application's message API without assuming a topology. send/receive are from the documented application's perspective. Deriving a receiver specification from a sender specification, or vice versa, is not recommended because channels and descriptions may differ. correlationId describes a tracing/matching location.
sources.input_inference: Retain viewpoint and unknown counterparts; do not reverse directions, assume servers are brokers, or correlate request/results by names alone.
sources.limitations: Correlation identifiers do not by themselves prove success, exactly-once processing, or required ordering. A request/reply contract is not an observed runtime outcome.

sources.title: Structurizr DSL — Implied relationships
sources.version: Mutable official documentation, observed 2026-11-19 UTC; no runtime version verified
sources.read_scope: Implied relationships and Configuring implied relationships; web lines 198–236
sources.observed: DSL creates implied relationships by default, including person-to-parent-system relations from person-to-contained-container relations. Configuration can disable them, and existing relationships affect the chosen strategy.
sources.input_inference: Keep explicit input relations distinct from tool-derived relations, with the derivation basis attached when supplied.
sources.limitations: DSL runtime was not executed. Derived overview relations can be useful; they do not establish additional direct communication or an execution event.

sources.title: Structurizr DSL — Identifiers
sources.version: Mutable official documentation, observed 2026-11-19 UTC; no runtime version verified
sources.read_scope: Identifiers and Identifier scope; web lines 198–257
sources.observed: Identifiers allow referencing model elements and relationships and are only needed when referenced. Flat identifiers are globally scoped; hierarchical element identifiers disambiguate identically named api elements. Relationship identifiers and groups do not follow the same hierarchical rule.
sources.input_inference: Reuse known identifiers or preserve source position/parent scope when the selected part has a repeated display name.
sources.limitations: These are DSL referencing rules, not a universal catalogue identity scheme. They do not justify introducing persistent IDs for every short purpose statement.
